title: Cause-and-effect table
subject: Geography
unit: Spring 1: Earning a living and globalisation
source: Seeded from geography/y9 lesson 11 (Cause-and-effect table (portal printable))
intro: Lesson 11: Why do employment patterns change? (3.4). To understand the reasons why the jobs people do change over time

questions.q: Explain how mechanisation changed farm jobs.
questions.a: Machines like combine harvesters did the work of many people, so fewer farm workers were needed
questions.model: Point: machines replaced farm workers. Evidence: a combine harvester does the work of many people. Explain: so far fewer people work in farming.

questions.q: Give one reason UK coal mining declined.
questions.a: For example: cheaper imported coal or switching to gas and renewables
People have more money to spend on services, and the population needs health and care

questions.q: Core: Copy and complete a cause-and-effect table for four reasons employment changes (reason, example, effect on jobs).
questions.a: Mechanisation: combine harvester: fewer farm jobs. Globalisation: clothes made in Asia: fewer UK factory jobs. Resources: coal: mines close. Wealth: more leisure: more service jobs
questions.model: Teacher shows row 1: 'Mechanisation; combine harvesters; fewer farm workers needed.'

questions.q: Extend: In the portal response box, predict two ways UK jobs may change by 2050, with reasons.
questions.a: For example: more automation in warehouses; more green energy and care jobs, with reasons

questions.q: Stretch: Is automation good or bad for workers? Give both sides.
questions.a: Good: removes dangerous, dull work and creates new jobs; bad: some lose jobs and need retraining
Machines and computers working by themselves
options: Machines and computers working by themselves

questions.q: Big question: will a robot do your future job?
questions.a: Some tasks will be automated, but jobs needing care, creativity and judgement are likely to remain; learning skills matters
